analysis.title: GS Basics: Brazil Surprise. Cost of Capital. Nets Down.
key_insights: Geopolitical relief at the open: the feared weekend escalation against Iran did not happen and diplomatic discussions continue. French protests were more contained than previous episodes, so a downgrade was avoided.

Brazil was the big surprise: Lula overturned a first-round deficit to win the election, with legal challenges looming. The result was far from prediction market expectations, so sizable pressure is expected across Brazilian assets and second-order exposures.
Asia semis largely caught down to where the US closed. Russell +2% and RSP +1.1% while Nasdaq -70bps and SOX -3.2%. VXN is elevated as tech implied vol reflects left-tail fears.
Bonds are catching a bid on growth concerns as AI capex runs into capital constraints.
Client backdrop remains very tough. US equities were sold for a third consecutive week, with the largest single-stock de-grossing since July. TMT sold about $20bn over two weeks.

Fundamental nets are at YTD lows but gross is still at the 63rd percentile. Global tech selling is -3.3σ over two weeks, with long sales outpacing short covers 3.4:1. Single stocks have been sold for six consecutive weeks.
Performance is poor across discretionary L/S, multi-strats and quants. Nets are low, but gross hurt last week (GSPESHRT, most vs least short in Europe, +3sd on a 60d lookback).

Hyperscalers: the author stays optimistic on demand but says the cost of capital has repriced with no obvious solve. Hyperscaler and data center credit spreads have widened across the capital structure, compounded by execution and refinancing risks.
Google, Microsoft and Amazon earnings this week are critical. The focus is how backlog converts into cloud revenue and how the next leg of capex is financed, not only whether capex intentions hold.

Capex financing scenarios: worst case is capex accelerating funded by expensive debt. Arguably worse is capex cut because financing is unavailable. Best case is capex rising with accelerating organic cash flow and a path to self-funding through 2027/28. Middle ground is flat/up capex with more equity financing, bad for hyperscaler equity and potentially good for credit.
Macro week: UK Budget risks including potential bank taxes (growing client interest in shorting the UK domestic consumer basket), China policy meetings, US 2yr/5yr/7yr supply, ECB, BOJ and FOMC.

The market expects the Fed to skip. The question is whether Warsh focuses on recent hot inflation or acknowledges how much financial conditions have tightened. AI and nominal growth camp are hoping for the latter.
Risk: hard to have high conviction and most clients are playing defense. Gross is tricky, performance is bleeding across strategies, and political events next week make a big swing difficult.

Energy remains critical. The author is confused by a policy that telegraphed escalation and let markets pre-price an energy shock, and suggests the strategy may be maximum military pressure ahead of a last-minute grand bargain, with talks ongoing.

Positioning, sentiment and performance are all severely constrained, with shorts squeezing and nothing working. It would not take much to stabilize risk, but there is no catalyst. Hyperscaler guidance and the Fed are the obvious opportunities, though risks are two-sided on both. The author is watching credit.
